summary: Stanford research system that researches a topic online and writes a full, cited Wikipedia-style article.

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: STORM (Synthesis of Topic Outlines through Retrieval and Multi-perspective Question Asking) is an LLM system from Stanford that researches a topic using web search and writes a long, Wikipedia-style article with citations. Co-STORM adds a collaborative mode where you take part in the research.
sixtySeconds.problem: Writing a well-sourced overview of a topic takes hours of research. STORM automates the research and outlining, giving you a cited first draft.
whoFor: Researchers and students starting a literature overview
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for a well-known research system with a Python package, multi-perspective questioning and support for many models via litellm.
requirements: A search API key such as Bing or You.com

overview: Install with pip install knowledge-storm, or clone the repo and install requirements in a conda environment for full control.

Put API keys in a secrets.toml file at the repo root (OpenAI key, retriever key such as BING_SEARCH_API_KEY, encoder type). Then run the example script with research, outline, article and polish steps.
The examples folder shows how to use other models or ground STORM on your own corpus, and how to run Co-STORM. MIT licensed.
limitations: Needs LLM and search API keys
